notes: Derived edit. Animal classes are individuals (instance_of), so the class can be a value of transmitted_by_class. The definitional premise "a disease is transmitted by an animal of whatever class its carrier belongs to" is the role chain transmitted_by ∘ instance_of ⊑ transmitted_by_class (OWL, so it also reaches an unnamed carrier). The record's bridges 'the arthropods that transmit the disease all belong to one class' (one_vector_class, for this disease only: the relation is many-valued in general) and 'no animal is both an insect and an arachnid' (one_animal_class) are firm. q1 reads "of the same class as X" over the two classes in play. (2026-10-31: one_vector_class was a general disjointness the record did not state.) Since 2026-10-31 the record says 'arthropods' (rats also spread plague); the carriers in this file are the arthropod vectors.

background.one_vector_class: plague : not ((transmitted_by_class value insect) and (transmitted_by_class value arachnid))

queries.ask: plague : transmitted_by_class some ({insect, arachnid} and inv(instance_of) value spiders)
